Ambiguous points:
(1) HookFailed has a single library construction site (constructs/mod.rs:1625). Otherwise it is meant to be built by consumer hook code, so its real report sites are in user code. I classed it as developer: the docs say it 'says nothing about the document', but the failure could also be environmental.
(2) ImplementationError: almost every site goes through ParseContext::implementation_error (constructs/mod.rs:1599–1606), which is called about 60 times across construct parsers. The direct ::new sites are in token/reader.rs:892 and 2053, token/scan.rs:561, 593 and 1234, scopes/mod.rs:1294, engine/language.rs:469 and constructs/mod.rs:1604. I listed only 5 of these.
(3) ScopeOpFailed is classed as developer, but the op's provider name could come from a document argument (for example a package-loading macro), so it could arguably be 'either'.
(4) UnresolvableCommand is classed as either because the default resolve_command hook answers Unresolved with a 'not implemented' detail.
(5) DeserializedCondition is an adapter. Its type IDENTIFIER is core.serialization.deserialized-condition, but each instance reports the written condition's identifier and message. Its fields are private.
(6) ForbiddenChar's `ch` field is serialized under the key "char".
(7) The field enums have no Display of their own. Their wire values come from ToDiagnosticValue (kebab-cased variant names), and the English wording sits in the parent condition's Display match.
(8) UnresolvableSourceReference's message includes ResolveError::message(), which the resolver writes, so that part of the text is not fixed.
(9) The DescentLimit* and ScopeOpFailed messages embed a `detail` produced elsewhere: DescentRefusal/DescentWarning detail from the DescentGuard, and the ScopeOpError Display.

I found 241 entries across 47 files. Each entry is one test function; when a test has several message asserts, the extra line numbers are in asserted_text. No rustdoc doctest in either crate compares message text.

The behavior-via-wording entries fall into these groups:
1. Which condition fired (about 70): "missing mandatory argument", "cannot resolve command", "unclosed group", environment conditions and similar. Switch to identifier(), with_identifier() or downcast_ref.
2. A condition field read through the message (about 25): the StrayGroupClose delimiter, OrphanEnd/MalformedBegin spelling, UnresolvableCommand detail, the "searched providers" list, did-you-mean suggestions. Downcast and compare the field.
